x: Eddie Short was second, Arthur Bruce, third, Martin Williamson, fourth. Eddie Short was third in the London University Inter Collegiate C.C.
The next two positions were filled by two junior members in Martin Williamson and Mike Heard. The former is up at Cambridge University while Mike has just been demobbed from the Royal Navy.

The holder of the title, Derrick Burfitt, was a non-runner as Derrick is not doing anything over the country this season in view of the coming Olympic Games, in which he is on the list of "possibles." A very close and interesting race was seen between Eddie Short, Martin Williamson and Arthur Bruce.
Ken Stimpson on the next stage to the Half Moon at Crawley, about 3½ miles—easily passed his opponent and handed over to Martin Williamson well in the lead.

Martin Williamson, our Junior Cross Country champion, is already busy on the track and recently won the Mile for St. Catherines College at the Cambridge University Freshmen's Meeting, and represented Cambridge University v.

Martin Williamson was selected to run for Cambridge University in the Mile Relay against Oxford, in the Universities Relay Meeting and he also represented Cambridge University in the Annual Oxford and Cambridge Track Meet at the White City in March.

The other positions were unchanged except that Mike Heard was hot on the heels of George Lucas, followed by Arthur Bruce and Martin Williamson, and it is pleasing to see these youngsters giving the senior members such a strong challenge.
A good field was seen in the 2 miles run and Eric Bishop, off 260 yds., was a good winner with Martin Williamson, off 180, second, and Lou Bush, off 300 yds., third.
As Cambridge had their scoring six in the first nine places, including our own Martin Williamson, who was 5th, they finished easy winners with 30 pts. against 57 pts. by Belgrave.

At the National cross-country championships at Great Barr, Birmingham, we were pleased to see Martin Williamson with his wife, and they are living at Leamington, but Martin does not find time for any running but is keenly interested in all the Club is doing.

Newcomers to the team were Tom Clinton, Ken Stimpson, Martin Williamson and Eddie Short. Twenty-five clubs competed in 1949 and we accomplished our second hat-trick of wins, thus achieving more wins in the nineteen races held than any other club.
